facts: The U.S. Department of Commerce finalized up to $1.61 billion in direct CHIPS Incentives funding for Texas Instruments, with disbursement tied to completion of project milestones.
The award supports more than $18 billion of TI investment through the end of the decade for three new facilities: two in Texas and one in Utah.

Commerce describes TI as a leading U.S. analog and embedded-processing manufacturer and says the projects expand domestic capacity for foundational current-generation and mature-node semiconductors used across electronic systems.
The supported projects are estimated to create more than 2,000 manufacturing jobs plus thousands of construction jobs.

risks.risk: CHIPS direct funding is milestone-based; announced award size does not mean all cash has already been received or that fab execution/utilization risk is eliminated.

unknowns.unknown: This source does not establish current fab utilization, incremental returns on new capacity, current valuation, or peer-relative economics; those remain Alpha underwriting work.
